P1.evidence: No setter on this call so nothing to read back. The first three minutes had no frame at all — the recording opens with the prospect describing his business and helicopter career, and drifts into a conversation about growing hair out. The frame arrived late and truncated, in the usual three-part form: 'I just want to get a good idea where you're [at]. Build out what it is that you really want. Then, if there's alignment, we can talk about the coaching. If not, that's fine, too.' No agreement was sought, and the prospect immediately took the agenda — 'I mean, yeah, go for it. You go into it, and then I'll let you know when I have questions.' The rep did recover the open question: 'what was it that you were hoping we could help you with? Let's start with them.' He never got the frame back, and the prospect ran the interview for the remaining twenty-eight minutes.

P2.evidence: One clean hit in nine. 'Are you training now or not really?' was asked and produced the walks, the meal delivery and the CrossFit-hybrid gym. Everything else was skipped or volunteered. Age came unprompted; height and weight were never taken even though the prospect was actively discussing body composition and had three competing body-fat readings in hand. No health conditions, no injuries, no movement limitations, no sleep, no energy. Diet was never asked — the entire Nutrition Solutions account was volunteered — which is a serious omission on a call where the prospect later challenged whether he needed the nutrition pillar at all. Work was covered only because the prospect opened with it.

P3.evidence: The six-month outcome question was asked and asked well — 'if we were to fast-forward six months into the future, what is it that you would say is the outcome?' — and returned a precise, numeric, entirely surface-level answer. Nothing was done with it. No bridge to why now, no what-does-moving-better-actually-do-for-you, no who-else-does-this-impact, no legacy or identity, no reflect-back. This is a 42-year-old business owner with two children half the week and thirteen years of professional flying behind him, and the deepest the call went was 15% body fat. The absence of P3d is the single largest missed opportunity on the tape: nobody ever asked why he booked this call now.

P4.evidence: No past-attempts question of any kind, despite the prospect having a rich and freely offered history — a P90X era, hard gym periods, prior kettlebell work, and 'I've had success in numerous other modes of fitness to get lean and cut and have my abs come out.' That last line is a direct statement that cheaper things have worked for him before, and it went unexamined. He also diagnosed his own root cause twice, unprompted — 'I'm one of those putter-around procrastinator' and 'I guess always it's commitment, right, which is something I got to work on internally' — and the second one was answered with 'Depends how bad you want it, dude.' That was the moment the call was available to win and it was returned as a shrug.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. The nearest move was a passive statement rather than a question: 'you have the ability, you're capable, it's possible, just depends really if you feel like you're ready and if you're ready to go all in is really what it is.' No two-year picture, nothing about what settling looks like, no why-not. With no cost of inaction established, a prospect whose stated barrier was commitment had nothing to weigh commitment against.

P6.evidence: No commitment check at any point, before or after the offer. Price was named at 00:11:11 — eight minutes into the call and immediately after a single question about training frequency — with no belief question and no all-in question. The prospect had not yet been asked why he wanted any of this. Everything after that point was him interrogating the product, which is the predictable shape of a call where the buyer was never asked to commit to an outcome first.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted. The rep described the mechanism once — 'you are just booking your onboarding call with Trevor once you process the payment' — but never asked for the business, never asked what the prospect wanted to do, and accepted a request for an email as the next step. Payment, onboarding, agreement and welcome steps were all out of scope.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger present but unusually favourable: the prospect raised the number and then removed it as a barrier himself — 'I can afford it, but it's not about that.' That is the isolation move handed over for free, and it should have redirected the whole conversation to what it actually was about. Instead the rep did the opposite of the play. He ran no isolation, asked nothing about finances, and responded to a stated non-price objection by progressively reducing the commitment: confirming a pause policy, then a $4,000 three-month tier, then a $1,200 one-month trial, then screen-sharing a $200/month self-guided product. The only scripted-adjacent move was the '6,000 reasons to commit' reframe. Discounting against an objection the prospect had explicitly disclaimed is the coaching point here, and it is a more serious error than any of the omissions.

The rep correctly diagnosed the state — 'It sounds like there's a level of certainty that you don't have that you want, and it's fine' — which is essentially the play's opening move, the certainty question, delivered as a statement. He then ran none of the five moves that follow. No pleasure-versus-pain, no bridge, no plane, no burned-before, no how-will-you-know-if-you-never-try. Having named the need for certainty he answered it commercially, with a cheaper trial, rather than working it. The prospect's actual certainty request was explicit and evidential — testimonials, before-and-afters, metrics from past clients — and it was promised by email rather than met on the call.

Trigger present in substance at the close: 'send me an email with just some of the breakdown or, you know, one month kind of thing, and we can go from there.' Not one OA move ran. No can-this-get-you-there, no what-makes-you-feel-it-can, no what's-actually-preventing-you-from-getting-started, no thinking-versus-deciding. The rep agreed to send collateral and closed with 'if you've something you want to pursue, hit me up. If not, it's fine.'

A cheaper alternative that plausibly works — the known second gap in the script, and here it arrived twice. Externally as Shredfast, a named UK competitor the prospect had researched and described as 'a similar number. It's less'. The rep handled that half reasonably, differentiating on the fact that buyers there get a layer of trained coaches and an app rather than the principal, which is a real and defensible distinction, although he weakened it by asserting the competitor uses steroids. Internally the same objection arrived as the company's own $200/month self-guided tier, and here the rep created the problem himself by volunteering it and then screen-sharing its contents. He had no framework for defending a 30x price gap and did not attempt one beyond 'the coaching is completely tailored to you.' The script needs a play for this and the absence is now costing deals with exactly the buyer profile the ICP describes.

Unbundling request with no scripted play: 'what if you don't need all the components like nutrition and all that kind of stuff because you've got it semi-dialed in?' The rep held the line on the system being integrated, which is the right instinct, but supported it with an anecdote about vegetarian Indian clients rather than with any reason why an already-solved nutrition input still needs coaching. He then undercut his own answer by offering a trial. The prospect never got an answer to what he actually asked.

notes: The thinnest process in the batch attached to the strongest prospect in it. One baseline check, one goals check, nothing in past attempts, nothing in consequence, nothing in commitment, and a price on the table at eight minutes. From that point the prospect controlled the call and conducted what amounted to due diligence, and the rep answered every question by making the offer smaller — pause policy, three-month tier, one-month trial, self-guided tier — against a buyer who had already said money was not the issue. The instruction for this rep is specific and inverted from the rest of the batch: with a core-ICP buyer, do less discounting and more discovery. He never asked why now, and he never asked for the business.
